All About
Foxes 🦊

A complete classroom lab built around the original Reading A–Z Level D book. Listen, decode, read, speak, write—and prove you can use the English with other animals.

🎧 Listening🧩 Phonics📖 Reading💬 Speaking✍️ Writing
Lesson 1 · 55–60 min

Hear + Decode + Read

Audio-only picture matching, word recognition and spelling, picture-only reading, simple retrieval.

Lesson 2 · 55–60 min

Organize + Speak + Write

Information structure, seasonal comparisons, old-animal transfer, mini nonfiction report.

5–7 Days Later · 15 min

Delayed Mastery Check

Without the original book: unseen listening/spelling prompts and a short transfer task.

How to use this lesson

Run this with the original book closed whenever the task says audio-only, no text, or retrieval. Divide the 23-word bank into manageable sets of 8–12 words per class; mastery develops through spaced reuse. The teacher can reveal answers only after students respond. All 23 user-specified words are covered in the Word Lab. Progress is saved in the current browser when you click Save Record.

The original book gives short, precise facts. A statement such as “Foxes only hunt at night” is not established by “mostly at night”; do not teach it as a proven fact or its logical opposite.

What this tests

Sound → meaning → visual recognition. Do not accept “I can read it when I see the word” as proof of listening mastery. Recycle the weak items in the next lesson.

02 / ALL 23 TARGET WORDS

Word Mastery Lab 🔤

Every word is trained through read aloud, listen & spell, and use in a sentence. Click a photo-word card to see a real photograph and practise READ → SPELL → USE. In SPELL mode, the word stays hidden but the photograph stays visible.

Word bank · 23

0 / 23 fully checked
Important morphology: point → pointy; bush → bushy; hunt → hunter; most → mostly. “Fur” is generally uncountable in this use. Do not make students memorize morphology terminology.
Target word01 / 23

📷 Real photograph · from the picture book
Photograph sources: vocabulary images for 21 entries are photographed foxes from the user-provided Reading A–Z book. The point and bush entries use Wikimedia Commons photographic images, with embedded picture-book fallback if the network is unavailable. For abstract language such as each / their / mostly, photographs give context, while the sentence clarifies usage.

Word-Family Detective

Make one new word from another
point → pointy

point to a picture → pointy face

bush → bushy

a bush → a bushy tail

hunt → hunter

Foxes hunt → Foxes are hunters

most → mostly

most of the time → mostly at night

03 / THE ORIGINAL BOOK

Read with Meaning 📖

First show the original photo without text. Then listen, echo, uncover the text and read independently.

Printed page 3 / 10 Classification
From the uploaded All About Foxes
Picture first → sound → sentence
Look at the picture. What do you notice?

Echo → Chunk → Independent Read

Teacher says: “They have / thin legs / and bushy tails.” Learner echoes each chunk, then reads the full sentence without help. Mark decoding errors separately from unfamiliar word meanings.

04 / BOOK CLOSED

Fact Retrieval & Paraphrase 💬

Ask a question without reopening the book. A good answer keeps the meaning; it does not need to copy every original word.

Question 1 / 8
Teacher observes how independently the learner answers
Use PEER: Prompt → Evaluate → Expand → Repeat. For example, “Long fur.” → “Foxes have long fur in winter.”
05 / NONFICTION READING ARCHITECTURE

Main Idea & Information Map 🗂️

Turn eight separate book facts into four information groups. This prepares students to write new animal reports.

Mission A · Which is the whole-book idea?

Choose one sentence that covers the whole book, not just one detail.

Mission B · Choose a fact

0 / 8

Then put it in the right category

Choose one fact, then click a category.

Precision Detective · Mostly is NOT only

Original book: They hunt mostly at night.

Does the book say foxes hunt ONLY at night?

Choose one.
“Mostly” does not prove “only.” The stronger statement is not established by the source, so don't label it a confirmed fact.
06 / MOVE BEYOND THE BOOK

Seasons, Speaking & Animal Transfer 🌿

First explain how a fox changes with the seasons. Then speak about other familiar animals without copying the text.

Tell me without reading the book

Compare

In summer, foxes have ______ fur.

In winter, foxes have ______ fur.

Each spring, foxes ______.

Think beyond the text

Why might long fur help a fox in winter?

This is an inference, not an answer directly stated in the book.

Possible inference: long fur may help keep foxes warm. Accept any relevant explanation. Do not grade this as direct retrieval.

Animal Detective · Transfer facts across books

The learner has read about foxes, spiders and earthworms. Hear a fact and choose the animal. Then say a whole sentence.

Listen, then choose Fox / Spider / Earthworm.
Suggested follow-ups: “Tell me one more fact about this animal.” “How is this animal different from a fox?” Accept basic but accurate sentences.
07 / OUTPUT FROM INPUT

Draw, Label & Write ✍️

Use the new words to make a fox picture and write an original mini nonfiction report.

Listen, Draw & Label

Listen to one instruction at a time. Draw the fox, then label its face, legs, fur and tail.

Press Next drawing instruction.
Pen

Write the body labels

Five-Sentence Fox Report

Type in complete English sentences. Try to use your own words.

Possible model:
Foxes are mammals. They have pointy faces, thin legs and bushy tails. Their fur can be different colors. They have short fur in summer and long fur in winter. Foxes are hunters, and they hunt mostly at night.

Accept shorter, accurate sentences at this stage.

Complete this 5–7 days after the lesson if possible, with the book closed. Tests both memory and transfer.

Mission B · Text Precision

Original book: Foxes hunt mostly at night. Which statement can we safely make?

Choose the statement best supported by the original book.

Mission C · Three Animals, One Report Structure

Choose a different familiar animal. Then write three accurate facts without looking at the old reader.

Choose an animal.

Spiders: eight legs; eat bugs; can climb; make silk; can live inside and outside. Earthworms: live in soil; have rings; can be different colors/sizes; help plants. Facts should come from previously read texts or prior learning, not guesses.

Mission D · Teacher Oral Rubric

What would count as mastery?

Not yet assessed

Strong performance = recognizable listening, accurate spelling, information retrieval, correct reading of mostly, and at least three independent animal facts in a new context.

7-Day Listening & Reuse Cycle

Day 1 · Look at the pictures and listen.

Day 2 · Echo 4–6 key sentences.

Day 3 · Listen with the book closed; retrieve 4 facts.

Day 4 · Hear paraphrased descriptions; choose pictures.

Day 5 · Audio-only questions; answer in sentences.

Day 6 · Use fox language with spiders or earthworms.

Day 7 · Complete final delayed mastery mission.
